title: Retain first occurrences throughout a list
description: ListWeave is a small in-memory library for arranging JSON list data. This snapshot contains unique(values). A duplicate-filtering refactor now misses repeats separated by other entries. Restore the documented contract. values is either a JSON list or None; other argument types are outside this task contract. All JSON numbers are finite and integers stay within the JavaScript safe range.

requirements.text: For a list values, unique returns the first member of each Python == equality class, in original first-occurrence order. Equality is recursive for lists and dictionaries; strings compare exactly without Unicode normalization, and Python numeric equality includes True == 1 and False == 0. Nested JSON values and None elements are supported. The empty list returns [].
For list input, unique leaves the caller list and all its nested lists and dictionaries unchanged, including when removing nonadjacent duplicates.
Passing None as values raises TypeError.

title: Preserve a final partial list block
description: This ListWeave snapshot exposes blocks(values, width), used to divide in-memory list data into consecutive display batches. A loop-bound regression drops a final short batch. Restore all documented behaviors. All inputs and outputs are JSON values; numbers are finite and integers are within JavaScript safe range.

requirements.text: For list values and a positive integer width, blocks returns consecutive nonempty sublists of at most width elements in original order. Every element appears exactly once. Include the final short block without padding; width 1 produces singleton blocks, and an empty values returns [].
For valid calls, blocks leaves values and its nested lists and dictionaries unchanged, including calls with a final partial block.

values must be a list and width must have Python type int, excluding booleans; any violation raises TypeError. With those types valid, zero or negative width raises ValueError, including when values is empty.

title: Honor signed cyclic list shifts
description: This ListWeave snapshot contains rotate(values, steps), an in-memory sequence reordering helper. A refactor that handles the shift magnitude lost the leftward direction of negative steps. Restore the documented signed rotation. Inputs and outputs are JSON values with finite numbers and JavaScript-safe integers.

requirements.text: For list values and integer steps, rotate moves elements cyclically right by steps positions when positive and left by -steps when negative, preserving relative cyclic order. Reduce steps modulo list length; zero and whole-length multiples keep the order, a singleton keeps its value, and an empty list returns [] for every integer steps.
For valid calls, rotate leaves values and all nested lists and dictionaries unchanged, including negative shifts that change the returned order.
values must be a list and steps must have Python type int, excluding booleans; any violation raises TypeError, even when values is empty.

title: Keep unpaired values during list weaving
description: This ListWeave snapshot provides interleave(left, right), which weaves two in-memory sequences for a paired display. A zip-based refactor loses entries when list lengths differ. Restore the full documented behavior for JSON data; numbers are finite and integers stay within JavaScript safe range.

requirements.text: For lists left and right, interleave returns left[0], right[0], left[1], right[1], and so on while both have elements, then all remaining elements of the longer list in their original order. Empty lists are supported, including both empty. Every occurrence is retained, even equal or nested JSON values.
For valid calls, interleave leaves both caller lists and all nested lists and dictionaries unchanged, including unequal-length inputs.
Both left and right must be lists; if either is any other JSON type, including None, raise TypeError before producing a result.

title: Count adjacent list runs independently
description: This ListWeave snapshot contains runs(values), a compact representation of consecutive repeated list items for in-memory display summaries. A counting refactor merged separate runs of the same value. Restore the adjacent-run contract for JSON data, with finite numbers and JavaScript-safe integers.

requirements.text: For list values, runs returns one {"value": first_item, "count": positive_integer} object for each maximal contiguous Python == run, in order. Nonadjacent equal values stay separate. Equality is recursive for lists and dictionaries, exact for strings without Unicode normalization, and includes Python numeric equality True == 1 and False == 0. Each run retains its first item as value; None and empty nested containers are supported. Empty input returns [].
For list input, runs leaves the caller list and all nested lists and dictionaries unchanged, including repeated values in separate runs.
A non-list values of any JSON type, including None, raises TypeError.

title: Repeated page marks fragment contiguous reading runs
description: The reading log receives repeated page marks after manual imports. Repair page_runs(pages) while retaining its inclusive, sorted run representation and validation behavior.

requirements.text: page_runs(pages) returns sorted inclusive [first,last] pairs covering exactly the distinct input page numbers. Consecutive integers belong to one run; gaps start new runs. Input order and duplicate occurrences do not affect the result. An empty list returns [].
The function must leave the supplied pages list unchanged, including element order and duplicate occurrences, on both successful returns and ValueError paths.

pages must be a list whose every element is a plain integer from 1 through 1000000 inclusive. Booleans, floats, strings (including Unicode), null, out-of-range integers and non-list outer values are invalid; raise ValueError for any invalid input.

title: Exact-capacity sessions split too early
description: Whole-chapter sessions unexpectedly split when their combined page count equals the configured limit. Repair chapter_sessions(chapter_lengths, limit) without changing input order or the handling of oversized chapters.

requirements.text: chapter_sessions(chapter_lengths, limit) returns lists of whole chapter lengths in original order, greedily filling each session while its sum stays <= limit. Flush a nonempty session before a chapter that would make its sum exceed limit. An individually oversized chapter must occupy its own session unchanged. Never emit empty sessions; empty input returns [].
The chapter_lengths list must remain unchanged on successful returns and ValueError paths, including when multiple chapters fit exactly into a session or a chapter is oversized.

chapter_lengths must be a list of plain integers from 1 through 1000000 inclusive, and limit must be a plain integer in the same range. Reject booleans, floats, strings (including Unicode), null, out-of-range integers and a non-list chapter_lengths value with ValueError.

title: Chapter boundary pages resolve to the wrong chapter
description: The reading position view has an off-by-one error at chapter endings. Repair locate_page(chapter_lengths, page), retaining one-based indices and the positions of zero-length chapters in chapter numbering.

requirements.text: locate_page(chapter_lengths, page) returns {"chapter": c, "page": p} for the chapter containing the one-based book page, with both c and p one-based. A chapter includes its last page. Zero-length chapters consume no book pages but retain their positions in chapter numbering. Return null when the book page exceeds the total length, including for empty/all-zero chapter lists.
The chapter_lengths list must be unchanged after a successful return or ValueError, preserving zero-length entries and their order.

chapter_lengths must be a list of plain integers from 0 through 1000000 inclusive; page must be a plain integer from 1 through 1000000 inclusive. Booleans, floats, strings (including Unicode), null, out-of-range values and a non-list chapter_lengths value must raise ValueError.

title: Later reading sessions replace earlier page totals
description: The book-club summary currently loses earlier sessions for a title. Repair reading_totals(records) while preserving exact title identity and the order in which titles first appear.

requirements.text: reading_totals(records) returns one {"book": title, "pages": sum} record for each distinct exact book string, ordered by first occurrence. Sum all page counts for that string. Title matching is case-sensitive and performs no trimming or Unicode normalization. Empty strings and zero totals remain represented. Empty input returns [].
The supplied records list and every record dictionary must remain unchanged on successful returns and ValueError paths, including duplicate-title aggregation.

records must be a list of dictionaries with exactly the keys "book" and "pages". book must be a string, with any Unicode content including an empty string allowed. pages must be a plain integer from 0 through 1000000 inclusive. Any invalid outer value, entry, key set, title type or page value (including booleans, floats and null) raises ValueError.

title: Half-percent progress ties round down unexpectedly
description: The progress badge uses the wrong rounding rule at exact half-percent values. Repair reading_percentage(completed, total) while retaining saturation and strict count validation.

requirements.text: For valid counts with completed < total, reading_percentage(completed, total) returns the nearest integer to 100 * completed / total, rounding an exact halfway value upward. In particular, zero completed pages returns 0. The result is a JSON integer.
For valid counts with completed >= total, return exactly 100, including counts beyond the planned total.

completed must be a plain integer from 0 through 1000000 inclusive, and total must be a plain integer from 1 through 1000000 inclusive. Reject booleans, floats, strings (including Unicode), null and any out-of-range value with ValueError.

title: Retain fill-down history across blank worksheet spans
description: Gridloom is an original stdlib-only worksheet library. This task concerns the named operation; retain all other functions. Inputs and outputs are JSON values. A valid worksheet is a list of lists whose cells are None or exact integers (booleans and floats are not integers). Integer inputs and all aggregate sums in scope are within the JavaScript safe range. No function may mutate any caller argument, including before raising an error. Empty rows and an empty worksheet are supported. Repair the reported regression while preserving the full contract below. The current fill-down refactor forgets earlier column values after blank spans.

requirements.text: fill_down(rows) replaces each explicit None cell with the most recent integer in the same column in any earlier input row, or leaves it None if no earlier integer exists. Explicit integers, including zero and negatives, remain unchanged. Carrying through consecutive None cells must keep the last integer.

Preserve the number and order of rows and the exact length of every row. Missing columns and empty rows do not clear earlier column history and do not gain new cells. An empty worksheet returns [], and empty rows remain [].

Reject a non-list worksheet, any non-list row, or any cell other than None or an exact integer with TypeError; this includes rejecting booleans, floats, strings (including Unicode), lists and objects as cells. Validate all rows, including rows after otherwise valid data.

title: Keep explicit empty cells during worksheet transposition
description: Gridloom is an original stdlib-only worksheet library. This task concerns the named operation; retain all other functions. Inputs and outputs are JSON values. A valid worksheet is a list of lists whose cells are None or exact integers (booleans and floats are not integers). Integer inputs and all aggregate sums in scope are within the JavaScript safe range. No function may mutate any caller argument, including before raising an error. Empty rows and an empty worksheet are supported. Repair the reported regression while preserving the full contract below. The current transpose helper treats explicit None cells as padding.

requirements.text: For transpose(rows, fill=0), every existing input cell at row r and column c must appear unchanged at output row c and column r, including explicit None, zero and negative integers. Preserve both coordinate orders.

The result has max input-row length rows (zero when there are no cells), each with len(rows) cells. Use fill only where the corresponding input row lacks that column. The default fill is 0; None is a permitted fill. Empty input or only empty rows returns [].

Reject a non-list worksheet, any non-list row, or any cell other than None or an exact integer with TypeError; this includes rejecting booleans, floats, strings (including Unicode), lists and objects as cells. Validate all rows, including rows after otherwise valid data. Also reject fill unless it is None or an exact integer, even when the worksheet is empty.

title: Include the final complete worksheet window
description: Gridloom is an original stdlib-only worksheet library. This task concerns the named operation; retain all other functions. Inputs and outputs are JSON values. A valid worksheet is a list of lists whose cells are None or exact integers (booleans and floats are not integers). Integer inputs and all aggregate sums in scope are within the JavaScript safe range. No function may mutate any caller argument, including before raising an error. Empty rows and an empty worksheet are supported. Repair the reported regression while preserving the full contract below. The complete-window boundary check drops the last band when it ends exactly at the worksheet boundary.

requirements.text: row_windows(rows, size, stride=1) returns each complete consecutive window of exactly size rows starting at indices 0, stride, 2*stride, and so on. Include a complete window ending exactly at len(rows). Preserve window order and each row and cell within it, including empty rows and None cells; overlapping windows are allowed.
Omit every incomplete trailing window. If rows is empty or size exceeds len(rows), return []. A stride larger than size may leave gaps and must not manufacture intermediate windows or a partial tail.

Reject a non-list worksheet, any non-list row, or any cell other than None or an exact integer with TypeError; this includes rejecting booleans, floats, strings (including Unicode), lists and objects as cells. Validate all rows, including rows after otherwise valid data. Require size and stride to be exact integers (not bool or float), otherwise TypeError. After type validation, either value <= 0 raises ValueError.

title: Count zero-valued worksheet cells as populated
description: Gridloom is an original stdlib-only worksheet library. This task concerns the named operation; retain all other functions. Inputs and outputs are JSON values. A valid worksheet is a list of lists whose cells are None or exact integers (booleans and floats are not integers). Integer inputs and all aggregate sums in scope are within the JavaScript safe range. No function may mutate any caller argument, including before raising an error. Empty rows and an empty worksheet are supported. Repair the reported regression while preserving the full contract below. A truthiness shortcut undercounts columns containing explicit zero cells.

requirements.text: column_summary(rows) returns one {"sum": integer, "count": integer} object per column, ordered from column zero through the longest row. sum is the signed integer sum of all present non-None cells in that column; missing cells and None contribute zero. A column with no integers has sum 0. Empty input or only empty rows returns [].

For each returned column, count is the number of present non-None cells in that column. Explicit zero and negative integers each count as one; missing cells and explicit None count as zero. A column with no integers has count 0.

Reject a non-list worksheet, any non-list row, or any cell other than None or an exact integer with TypeError; this includes rejecting booleans, floats, strings (including Unicode), lists and objects as cells. Validate all rows, including rows after otherwise valid data.

title: Limit worksheet row deduplication to consecutive runs
description: Gridloom is an original stdlib-only worksheet library. This task concerns the named operation; retain all other functions. Inputs and outputs are JSON values. A valid worksheet is a list of lists whose cells are None or exact integers (booleans and floats are not integers). Integer inputs and all aggregate sums in scope are within the JavaScript safe range. No function may mutate any caller argument, including before raising an error. Empty rows and an empty worksheet are supported. Repair the reported regression while preserving the full contract below. The current deduplication optimization removes later runs that happen to match earlier rows.

requirements.text: collapse_rows(rows) keeps exactly one representative row from each maximal consecutive run of equal rows. Rows are equal only when they have the same length and corresponding cells are equal, with None distinct from every integer. Preserve all cell positions and values; different rows must not collapse merely because their length or sum matches.

Preserve the order of runs and retain a row when an unequal row separates it from an earlier equal row, including separated empty rows or None-containing rows. Only neighboring equal rows collapse. An empty worksheet returns [].

Reject a non-list worksheet, any non-list row, or any cell other than None or an exact integer with TypeError; this includes rejecting booleans, floats, strings (including Unicode), lists and objects as cells. Validate all rows, including rows after otherwise valid data.

title: Restore adjacency-aware band coalescing
description: RibbonPlan stores a ribbon as an ordered list of colored bands. A recent aggregation refactor changed coalesce so separated occurrences of a color lose their positions. Restore the retained ordered-band contract.

requirements.text: coalesce(bands) returns a list of color/length records obtained by replacing each maximal consecutive run of exactly equal color strings with one record whose length is their sum. Preserve run order and label text. Equal colors separated by another color remain separate. An empty input returns [].

bands must be a list of at most 1000 dictionaries, each with exactly color and length keys. color must be a nonempty string; Unicode, case and spaces are literal label content. length must be an integer from 1 through 1000000, excluding booleans. Invalid bands, records, keys or field values raise ValueError, including None, an empty color, and noninteger lengths.

The function must leave the caller's bands list and every contained record unchanged, both on a successful return and when raising ValueError. This includes ordinary nonempty calls whose result differs from the input.

title: Restore partial-band span extraction
description: RibbonPlan extracts material spans using integer positions measured from the start of the ribbon. An optimization stopped including partial bands at span edges. Restore the established half-open extraction behavior.

requirements.text: slice_span(bands, start, stop) returns the portion in the half-open interval [start, stop), using cumulative band lengths as coordinates. Emit each positive overlap in original order with its color and overlap length. Retain original band boundaries even for neighboring equal colors. Clip positions beyond the total length. Empty input, start == stop, or start at or beyond the total returns [].

bands must be a list of at most 1000 dictionaries, each with exactly color and length keys. color must be a nonempty string; Unicode, case and spaces are literal label content. length must be an integer from 1 through 1000000, excluding booleans. Invalid bands, records, keys or field values raise ValueError, including None, an empty color, and noninteger lengths. start and stop must be integers excluding booleans, each from 0 through 1000000000, with start <= stop; otherwise raise ValueError.

The function must leave the caller's bands list and every contained record unchanged, both on a successful return and when raising ValueError. This includes ordinary nonempty calls whose result differs from the input.

title: Restore whole-pattern tile order
description: RibbonPlan tiles a short ribbon pattern for assembly planning. A loop refactor now repeats each band separately and changes the pattern order. Restore whole-pattern repetition and its retained boundaries.

requirements.text: tile(bands, count) returns count consecutive copies of the complete band sequence, in that order, with each output record containing the original color and length. Preserve every original band boundary and every boundary between copies, including neighboring equal colors; do not multiply lengths or coalesce bands. count == 0 or empty bands returns [].

bands must be a list of at most 1000 dictionaries, each with exactly color and length keys. color must be a nonempty string; Unicode, case and spaces are literal label content. length must be an integer from 1 through 1000000, excluding booleans. Invalid bands, records, keys or field values raise ValueError, including None, an empty color, and noninteger lengths. count must be an integer from 0 through 1000, excluding booleans; otherwise raise ValueError. Validate bands even when count is zero.

The function must leave the caller's bands list and every contained record unchanged, both on a successful return and when raising ValueError. This includes ordinary nonempty calls whose result differs from the input.

title: Restore first-use order in material totals
description: RibbonPlan summarizes material quantities in the order colors first appear on a pattern. A presentation refactor sorts the totals by color and disrupts that retained order. Restore the summary contract.

requirements.text: color_totals(bands) returns one color/length record for every distinct exact color string, ordered by that color's first appearance in bands. length is the sum of all input lengths for that color, including separated occurrences. Preserve label text; case variants and differently spaced strings remain distinct. Empty input returns [].

bands must be a list of at most 1000 dictionaries, each with exactly color and length keys. color must be a nonempty string; Unicode, case and spaces are literal label content. length must be an integer from 1 through 1000000, excluding booleans. Invalid bands, records, keys or field values raise ValueError, including None, an empty color, and noninteger lengths.

The function must leave the caller's bands list and every contained record unchanged, both on a successful return and when raising ValueError. This includes ordinary nonempty calls whose result differs from the input.

title: Restore material-distance ribbon rotation
description: RibbonPlan rotates a pattern so a chosen material position becomes its new start. A simplification interpreted the offset as a band count. Restore the distance-based rotation used by layout planning.

requirements.text: rotate(bands, offset) rotates left by offset material units modulo the sum of band lengths; negative offsets therefore rotate right. Cut within a band when needed: output its remaining suffix, subsequent bands, preceding bands, then its positive prefix. Preserve every preexisting boundary and the new cut boundary; never coalesce equal colors. A cut exactly at a boundary produces no zero-length record. Zero or a multiple of total length retains the sequence. Empty input returns [].

bands must be a list of at most 1000 dictionaries, each with exactly color and length keys. color must be a nonempty string; Unicode, case and spaces are literal label content. length must be an integer from 1 through 1000000, excluding booleans. Invalid bands, records, keys or field values raise ValueError, including None, an empty color, and noninteger lengths. offset must be an integer from -1000000000 through 1000000000, excluding booleans; otherwise raise ValueError, even for empty bands.

The function must leave the caller's bands list and every contained record unchanged, both on a successful return and when raising ValueError. This includes ordinary nonempty calls whose result differs from the input.

title: Keep every contribution when consolidating shopping rows
description: The pantry.py helpers serve one small batch-preparation planner. A row consolidation refactor now loses contributions for repeated ingredients. Repair aggregate_items(rows). The supported input is a list of at most 100 rows, each exactly a mapping with item (any Unicode string, including empty) and units (a whole-number JSON value from 0 through 1000000). Item equality is exact string equality, including case and Unicode composition. Whole-number JSON values mean finite integral numbers after JSON transport, excluding booleans; no Python int-versus-float distinction is promised. None/null, nonintegral numbers, other shapes, and inputs outside the stated bounds are outside this retained contract.

requirements.text: Return one {"item": name, "units": total} row for each distinct exact input item, summing units across all occurrences. Keep a row even when its total is zero. An empty input returns [].
The output rows appear in the order of each item's first occurrence in the input, regardless of alphabetic order or later occurrences.
Leave the input list and every input row mapping unchanged in content, including on calls that consolidate repeated items.

title: Avoid zero-sized batches at exact capacity boundaries
description: The same pantry.py planner partitions separate preparation orders. An arithmetic refactor creates an extra empty batch when an amount exactly fills its containers. Repair split_batches(amounts, limit). amounts is a list of at most 100 whole-number JSON values from 0 through 1000; limit is a whole-number JSON value from 1 through 100. Each amount is a separate order and must not be pooled with adjacent orders. Whole-number JSON values mean finite integral numbers after JSON transport, excluding booleans; no Python int-versus-float distinction is promised. None/null, nonintegral numbers, other shapes, and inputs outside the stated bounds are outside this retained contract.

requirements.text: For each positive amount, return an inner list of limit-sized batches followed by one remainder batch only when the remainder is positive. The inner list sums to that amount; no batch is zero. Preserve the outer order, and partition each amount independently.
A zero amount produces an empty inner list in its original position. An empty amounts list produces an empty outer list.
Do not change the content or order of the input amounts list while computing the batches.

title: Include requested ingredients absent from the inventory
description: The pantry.py planner compares a requested shopping mapping with current inventory. An inventory membership filter accidentally omits ingredients that are entirely absent. Repair plan_shortfall(requested, available). Both inputs are mappings with at most 100 keys; keys are arbitrary Unicode strings (including empty), matched exactly and case-sensitively; values are whole-number JSON quantities from 0 through 1000000. Whole-number JSON values mean finite integral numbers after JSON transport, excluding booleans; no Python int-versus-float distinction is promised. None/null, nonintegral numbers, other shapes, and inputs outside the stated bounds are outside this retained contract.

requirements.text: For every requested item that is also present in available, its returned quantity is max(requested quantity minus available quantity, 0), including an explicit zero when stock meets or exceeds demand.
The output has exactly the requested keys. An item absent from available uses zero available units; available-only keys never appear. An empty request returns {}.
Leave both requested and available mappings unchanged in content, including when demand exceeds stock or an item has no stock entry.

title: Round fractional preparation units upward
description: The pantry.py planner rescales indivisible ingredient units, such as scoops. A rounding refactor sometimes underestimates the units needed. Repair rescale_units(recipe, from_servings, to_servings). recipe is a mapping of at most 100 arbitrary Unicode ingredient strings (including empty) to whole-number JSON quantities from 0 through 1000000. from_servings is a whole-number JSON value from 1 through 1000; to_servings is from 0 through 1000. Whole-number JSON values mean finite integral numbers after JSON transport, excluding booleans; no Python int-versus-float distinction is promised. None/null, nonintegral numbers, other shapes, and inputs outside the stated bounds are outside this retained contract.

requirements.text: For a positive target serving count, retain every recipe key and return the least integer greater than or equal to units * to_servings / from_servings for each key. An original zero quantity remains zero.
With to_servings equal to zero, retain all recipe keys with quantity zero. An empty recipe returns {} for every supported serving count.
Do not change the recipe mapping in content, including when scaling changes one or more ingredient quantities.

title: Apply ingredient substitutions once and simultaneously
description: The pantry.py planner can substitute ingredient names before quantity planning. A duplicated mapping pass turns a single selected replacement into a second replacement. Repair substitute_items(items, replacements). items is a list of at most 100 Unicode strings; replacements is a mapping of at most 100 Unicode string keys to Unicode string values. Empty strings, repeated names, self-replacements and cycles in the map are supported. Exact string equality is used; no case or Unicode normalization occurs. None/null and all other shapes are outside this retained contract.

requirements.text: At each original input position whose string is a replacement key, emit that key's direct mapped value exactly once. Preserve positions and duplicates; a mapped value must not be looked up again, even when it is itself a key.
At positions whose original string is absent from replacements, emit the original string unchanged, including case and Unicode composition. An empty items list returns [].
Leave both the items list and the replacements mapping unchanged in content, including when one or more names are replaced.

title: Preserve exact material labels while consolidating workshop requirements
description: The material-line consolidation helper has started treating differently cased labels as one item. Restore its retained public contract. Inputs and results are JSON arrays of [label, units] pairs. All input integer values and all derived output totals in the supported domain remain within the JavaScript safe-integer range (absolute value at most 9007199254740991). Input combinations requiring an output total outside that range are out of contract; no additional exception behavior is promised for them.

requirements.text: combine_materials(lines) returns one [label, total_units] pair for each distinct label, summing all of its units. Labels compare by exact string equality, including case, Unicode code points and the empty string. Output follows first appearance of each label; retain labels whose total is zero. Empty input returns [].

lines must be a list of two-element lists. Each label must be a string and each units value a nonnegative integer; booleans and fractional numbers are invalid. A wrong container, pair length or field type raises TypeError; negative integer units raise ValueError. Validate every line, including zero-unit lines.
The supplied list and its nested pairs must remain unchanged on both a successful call and a validation exception.

title: Consume completed instruction occurrences only once
description: A completion-accounting regression removes every occurrence of a repeated instruction label. Restore the occurrence-based behavior used by workshop progress views.

requirements.text: remaining_steps(planned, completed) returns the planned labels left after consuming one earliest still-unconsumed equal planned occurrence per completed label. Compare strings exactly, including Unicode, case and empty labels. Preserve the original order of survivors. Extra completed occurrences and absent labels are ignored; empty planned returns [] and empty completed returns planned values.
Both arguments must be lists containing only strings; otherwise raise TypeError. Validate both entire lists even when planned is empty or a completed label would not match any planned label.
Both supplied lists must remain unchanged on success and on a validation exception.

title: Keep separated operation runs distinct in compact instruction displays
description: The compact instruction formatter has begun combining matching labels from separate sections. Restore adjacent-run formatting without changing the input sequence.

requirements.text: operation_runs(labels) returns [label, positive_count] pairs for maximal consecutive runs, in sequence order. Equal labels separated by any different label form separate output rows. Equality is exact string equality, including case, Unicode code points and empty strings. Empty input returns [].
labels must be a list whose every member is a string; otherwise raise TypeError. Do not coerce numbers, booleans, null, nested lists or objects into labels.
The supplied labels list must remain unchanged on successful formatting and on a validation exception.

title: Allow a workshop tray to reach its exact capacity
description: Tray planning now opens another tray when adding an item would exactly fill the current tray. Restore the documented contiguous greedy grouping, including zero-unit placeholders.

requirements.text: batch_units(units, capacity) processes amounts in their original order. Append each amount to the current batch when its resulting sum is at most capacity; otherwise start a new batch containing that amount. Return the resulting nonempty batches without reordering or dropping amounts, including zeros. Empty units returns [].

units must be a list of integers and capacity a positive integer. Booleans and fractional numbers are invalid. Wrong container or numeric types raise TypeError. Nonpositive capacity or any amount below zero or above capacity raises ValueError. Validate every amount before returning a result.
The supplied units list must remain unchanged on both success and a validation exception.

title: Use the requested final position when moving a workshop step
description: Moving an instruction toward the end currently places it one slot early. The editor API defines destination as an index in the final sequence, and callers retain their original sequence for undo previews.

requirements.text: reposition_step(steps, source, destination) returns a reordered list with the original source element at the destination index in the final list. Keep the relative order of every other element. Positions are zero based; source equal to destination returns the same values. Retain all string contents exactly, including duplicate, empty and Unicode labels.

steps must be a list of strings and source and destination must be integers, excluding booleans and fractional values; wrong types raise TypeError. Both positions must be at least zero and less than the length of steps; otherwise raise ValueError. Thus an empty list has no valid positions, and negative positions are not Python-style offsets.
The supplied steps list must remain unchanged on both a successful move and a validation exception.
